content:
The [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. What your investments could be worth — initial amount, monthly contributions and growth. Enter your initial investment, monthly contribution, expected annual return, years invested and compounding and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

An investment calculator projects what a portfolio could be worth: your starting amount, regular monthly contributions and an assumed annual return, compounded over time. It splits the result into what you put in and what growth added, so you can see how much of the final figure came from compounding rather than from your own pocket. Returns are never guaranteed — the calculator assumes a steady rate for illustration, while real markets rise and fall.

## How to use the Investment Calculator

Start by entering your initial investment, then entering your monthly contribution, entering your expected annual return (%), entering your years invested and finally choosing your compounding from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your starting investment — the lump sum you begin with.
2. Add your monthly contribution, or leave it at 0 for a one-off investment.
3. Enter the expected annual return and the number of years, then choose how often returns compound.
4. Compare the future value with your total contributions to see how much growth did the work.

## Formula

Future value = initial amount × (1 + r/n)^(n×t) + monthly contribution × the future value of a regular series at the same rate. r is the annual return, n the compounding periods per year, t the years.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Invest $10,000, add $300 a month and earn 7% compounded monthly for 20 years: the total reaches about $196,665. You contributed $82,000, so growth added about $114,665 — more than half the final value. Try the same figures in the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Initial investment: 10000, Monthly contribution: 300, Expected annual return: 7 %, Years invested: 20, Compounding: Monthly), the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) returns Future value: 196,665.39, Total contributions: 82,000, Investment growth: 114,665.39, Growth as % of total: 58.3%. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Compounding vs contributions

Over short periods, your contributions do most of the work — the balance grows mainly because you keep adding money. Over long periods the balance flips: growth on earlier growth starts to dominate, and by year 20 of a steady plan the investment earnings can exceed everything you paid in. That is why starting early matters more than investing large amounts late: time in the market is what lets compounding take over.

## What return should you assume?

A diversified stock portfolio has historically returned around 7–10% a year before inflation, and about 5–7% after inflation. Bonds and savings accounts return much less. The calculator assumes a single steady rate, but real returns vary year to year — a year of −20% followed by +20% does not leave you where you started. Use a conservative rate, and treat the result as a range rather than a promise.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Increase contributions with each pay rise — even 1% a year adds up over decades.
- Fees matter: a 1% annual fee can take roughly a quarter of your returns over 30 years.
- Reinvest dividends and interest so they compound too.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the return guaranteed?

No. Markets move up and down, and a steady 7% every year does not happen in real life. The calculator shows what a constant return would produce, so treat it as an illustration, not a forecast. Try it with your own numbers in the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Should I use a return before or after inflation?

For a figure in today's money, use a real (after-inflation) return of about 4–5%. For the nominal future amount, use 7–8%. Mixing the two is the most common mistake with these calculators. Try it with your own numbers in the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How is this different from a compound interest calculator?

They share the same maths. This one is framed around investing — monthly contributions and the split between what you paid in and what growth added — while the compound interest calculator also covers savings deposits and interest earned. Try it with your own numbers in the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Investment Calculator use?

Future value = initial amount × (1 + r/n)^(n×t) + monthly contribution × the future value of a regular series at the same rate. r is the annual return, n the compounding periods per year, t the years. You can see it in action in the [Investment Calculator](/investment-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Investment Calculator?

Just Initial investment, Monthly contribution, Expected annual return, Years invested and Compounding. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
